title: Chapter / Scene Metadata Compatibility Layer
goal: Add a metadata-only chapter and scene compatibility layer while preserving legacy flat Markdown scene files and owner-authored scene prose.
why_now: Project creation, selector/library, and frontend project switching precede chapter/scene metadata in the Phase 7 sequence; the active frontier now points to PHASE7-IMPL-004.

include: Inventory current scene route, storage, frontend API, UI, and test assumptions.
Plan metadata reads that preserve legacy scenes/{scene_id}.md compatibility.
Plan separate chapter and scene metadata writes that do not rewrite scene bodies.
Plan route and fallback tests for metadata-backed and legacy standalone scenes.
Plan frontend display of metadata-backed titles/order only after backend read compatibility exists.
exclude: Runtime app implementation in this enrichment artifact task.
Backend behavior changes during artifact generation.
Frontend behavior changes during artifact generation.
Owner-authored prose rewrites or generated prose.
Story Check, Ollama, live model calls, extraction tools, Dramatica-specific logic, OMI promotion, memory/canon mutation, and training data changes.

quality_notes: CCE evidence was repaired by clearing a polluted index and rebuilding with scoped paths only.
Graphify output was noisy and should be treated as weak topology evidence only.
AI Context is fallback status evidence only because task mode writes to a shared path.
Generated context and evidence artifacts are supporting evidence, not roadmap authority.

acceptance_criteria: Legacy scenes/{scene_id}.md files remain readable and writable through existing compatibility paths.

Metadata writes and ordering operations do not rewrite owner-authored scene Markdown bodies.
Route and helper tests cover metadata-backed scenes and legacy fallback behavior.
Frontend metadata display remains conditional on supported backend responses and does not generate prose.
